name: Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses
description:
## Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses

This is a casual pair-programming meetup for developers experimenting with Claude Code, Codex, and agentic coding workflows.
There is no formal presentation and no fixed curriculum. Bring a laptop, a repository, a side project, or a workflow you want to test. We will work in small groups, compare approaches, debug problems, and share what is working.

Possible areas to explore include:

* Building iterative coding-agent loops
* Comparing Claude Code and Codex on the same task
* Designing graph-based agent workflows
* Creating reusable coding harnesses
* Managing context across large repositories
* Running tests and validating agent-generated changes
* Using sandboxes, permissions, and approval steps
* Coordinating subagents or parallel tasks
* Measuring latency, token usage, cost, and completion quality
* Debugging failed or incomplete agent runs

You do not need to be an expert in either tool. This meetup is for people who want hands-on time to experiment, pair with other developers, and learn through building.
Bring something you are working on, or join someone else’s project.
Hosted by **Coffee & Code Philadelphia**.

name: OG Coffee&Code Coding!
description:
# ☕ The OG Coffee&Code Meetup

### A Blockspace Community × Coffee&Code Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”
This is **The OG Coffee&Code**—the meetup that started it all, now presented in collaboration with the **Blockspace Community**.
No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

## What this meetup is

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

## What this meetup is not

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

## How it works

1. Show up
2. Grab coffee ☕
3. Open your laptop, notebook, or sketchpad
4. Work at your own pace
5. Chat when you want and focus when you need
6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

## Who should attend

* Software engineers and data professionals
* Students and self-learners
* Founders and indie hackers
* Designers, tinkerers, and technologists
* Members of the Blockspace and Coffee&Code communities
* Anyone who enjoys building things with other humans

Whether this is your first Coffee&Code, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.
This collaboration brings together two communities around a shared goal: creating a relaxed, supportive space where people can build, learn, and connect.

**Come for the code.**
**Stay for the community.**
**Leave caffeinated. ☕🚀**

name: Adapting Your Data Strategy for AI
description:
***PLEASE REGISTER ON THE [WEBSITE](https://damaphila.starchapter.com/meetinginfo.php?id=50&ts=1782589865) TO OBTAIN ACCESS TO THE BULDING AND TO PAY FOR YOUR TICKET.***

Breakfast and lunch are included.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the industry, and successful AI needs a strong data foundation. When building your Data Strategy, it can be challenging to balance when to embrace AI and when the foundational aspects of data management, business intelligence, and data governance come into play. This presentation will include how to balance both innovation and foundation with practical, business-focused approaches to building an effective strategy and roadmap.
Topics include:

* Prioritizing AI and Analytics Use Cases
* Aligning AI with Data Management and Data Governance
* Building the Right Team - Roles and Responsibilities
* Developing an Effective Roadmap

**Donna Burbank** will be speaking on this topic. A recognized industry expert in data management with over 25 years of experience helping organizations enrich their business opportunities through data. She is currently the Managing Director of Global Data Strategy, Ltd., where she assists organizations around the globe in driving value from their data. Donna speaks regularly at industry conferences, she has co-authored several books on Data Management, and is a regular contributor to industry publications.
**Securing Your Data for AI**
**Session Description**
AI changes what enterprise data does. Beyond reporting and analytics, data now directly shapes model behavior, retrieval, recommendations, automation, and agent actions — making data governance a security concern. This session uses LLM04 2026: Data and Model Poisoning as an industry reference point to examine how poisoning risk enters through untrusted sources, manipulated content, stale knowledge, unsafe feedback loops, and AI-accessible data that is treated as more authoritative than it should be. The session will connect these risks to the governance controls required to secure data for AI systems.
**Additional Topics**

* How AI expands the enterprise data attack surface
* How poisoned or manipulated content affects RAG retrieval and recommendations
* How compromised fine-tuning sets and feedback loops degrade model behavior
* Source trust, provenance, and authority for AI-accessible data
* Ingestion controls and lifecycle management for AI pipelines
* Vulnerability identification and testing specific to AI data flows
* Mapping LLM04 2026 to practical data governance decisions

**Mark Roxberry** will be speaking on the topics. He is a trusted consultant in AI security and intelligent systems architecture with over 20 years of experience helping organizations navigate the intersection of data, risk, and emerging AI. He is Principal Consultant for Security and Intelligent Solutions at Database Solutions Inc. and holds CISSP and CEH certifications. Mark works with clients across healthcare, gaming, financial services, and other regulated industries. He leads the OWASP HACTU8 AI security testing project and the OWASP LLM04 Working Group, speaks regularly on AI governance and secure architecture, and focuses on making enterprise AI capabilities useful, testable, and governable in production environments.

​​​This time, we're back at **Delve's** office on Arch Street.

​*Hardware Meetups happen across 30+ cities monthly and help bring together different professionals to connect and meet each other.*

​**We will have a great set of featured speakers for the evening!:**

* ​[Dan Lykens](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlykens/?utm_source=luma), Electromechanical Engineer at [Production Systems Automation](https://www.psasystems.com/?utm_source=luma). Dan is a multidisciplinary engineer and entrepreneur with over a decade of experience in electromechanical systems, PCB design, and product development. At PSA, he leads defense-focused R&D projects, specializing in rugged electronics. Dan combines deep technical proficiency in PCB design, CAD modeling, and advanced prototyping techniques.
* ​A presenter from [Viam](https://viam.com/?utm_source=luma), a software platform for building, deploying, and managing robotics applications. Write control logic using a Viam SDK in your language of choice, with well-defined APIs for hardware and services. Treat hardware as a single machine in the cloud. Develop application code from anywhere. The same application code scales from the first prototype to a global fleet. Viam makes the physical world programmable.
* Dan Marcq, Client Partner and Senior Director of Electrical & Software Engineering at [Delve](http://www.delve.com/). Dan leads the development of complex hardware and connected systems from early strategy through commercialization. Since joining Delve in 2019, he has led multidisciplinary programs spanning electrical engineering, embedded systems, robotics, sensing, controls, and software for medical devices and other advanced products.

​**Thank you to our partners!:**

​We’re excited to welcome **[Efinix](https://www.efinixinc.com/index.html?utm_source=luma)** as a sponsor of our next Philadelphia Hardware Meetup!
Efinix manufactures the world’s most efficient FPGAs. Delivering low power, high performance and small physical size, Efinix FPGAs offer fast time to market in a cost-effective footprint. Efinix offers three families of FPGAs from the entry level Trion family that prioritizes I/O and connectivity to the Titanium family that offer high speed transceivers and high compute capability for industrial, edge and highly accelerated AI applications. The portfolio spans 4,000 logic elements up 375,000 logic elements and includes SiP offering with Flash and system memory in the same FPGA package. These highly integrated solutions reduce design complexity, increase available I/O and further speed time to market. The Efinix Efinity tool suite is freely available and delivers an intuitive RTL to bit-stream capability while supporting a rich IP library and software compilers for the suite of Sapphire RISC-V processors available as both hard IP and soft macros across the Efinix portfolio.
Efinix FPGAs have been widely adopted in a broad array of markets from industrial automation , communications, medical, automotive and test and measurement. To find out more about Efinix products and markets, visit [www.efinixinc.com](http://www.efinixinc.com/ "http://www.efinixinc.com").
Thank you to Efinix for supporting the Philadelphia hardware community and helping bring local engineers, founders, and product developers together.

description:

**Event Overview**
AI is transforming how healthcare and life sciences organizations discover drugs, run clinical trials, analyze data and develop new medical technologies. But innovation is also creating demand for talent that can bridge technology, science, clinical operations and regulatory requirements.

This session explores where technology professionals can find opportunity across the life sciences ecosystem—and which skills can transfer from traditional tech roles into this rapidly evolving market.

**What You'll Learn**

* Where technology and AI are driving growth across life sciences and digital health
* Why demand is shifting toward cross-functional technology + science talent
* High-demand skills across clinical operations, biometrics, data, AI/ML and regulatory functions
* How can tech professionals take their experience into life sciences
* Emerging roles and the H2 2026 hiring and investment outlook

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.
